items.title: Tyrese Maxey Emerging As 76ers' Go-To Option In Clutch Time
items.summary: Tyrese Maxey has become the Philadelphia 76ers' closer as they have begun a new phase following the offseason acquisitions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Maxey is the least decorated of the team's four All-Stars, but he has emerged as the clear No. 1 option late in games, and league executives told ESPN that his teammates already trust him in fourth quarters. Philadelphia is 7-0 in games that reach clutch time, defined as the score being within five points in the final five minutes. That perfect mark has driven the Sixers' league-best 8-1 record. Maxey ranks third in the league with 21 points in 19 clutch minutes. An Eastern Conference executive credited Maxey for the late-game success. "It's Maxey," said an East executive. "He's making them go and you can see he already has all of their trust in fourth quarters. LeBron definitely trusts him and they've already really developed a nice two-man game that stresses defenses." Another executive pointed to LeBron James' influence on Maxey's growth. "LeBron brings a lot of things when he comes to your team," said another East executive. "And we've seen it before, he raises everyone's level. Maxey was already a great player, but he's also raised his level and some of that has to be having LeBron there." Nick Nurse described the 26-year-old guard's fourth-quarter presence. "He comes and gets the first bucket or two of the fourth and ... 'Here it comes, here it comes,'" said Nurse. "In an incredibly humble way, he just seems like he knows he's really good. I don't know if I've sensed that until this year." The Sixers rank in the bottom 10 in offensive efficiency but boast a top-three defense. They are 4-0 on the road, including wins over the New York Knicks and Detroit Pistons.

items.title: Kevin McCullar Jr., Raptors Agree To Two-Way Deal
items.summary: The Toronto Raptors signed guard Kevin McCullar Jr. to a Two-Way contract. McCullar appeared in 21 games as a Two-Way player with the New York Knicks last season. He averaged 2.4 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 7.4 minutes while shooting 42.6% from the field. Over 14 games in the G League, McCullar averaged 16.8 points, 6.2 assists, 5.4 rebounds, 2.0 steals and 1.0 blocks. The Phoenix Suns selected McCullar 56th overall in the 2024 NBA draft before trading his rights to New York. He holds career averages of 2.2 points and 1.4 rebounds in 25 games over two seasons with the Knicks. The San Antonio native played three seasons at Texas Tech before transferring to Kansas. McCullar earned First Team All-Big 12 honors as a fifth-year senior with the Jayhawks in 2023-24.
